title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 39
paragraphs: This, then, is one of the peninsulas. The other, beginning from the land of the Persians, stretches to the Erythraian Sea, including Persia, next Assyria, and after Assyria Arabia. This ends—or rather is commonly supposed to end—at the Arabian gulf, into which Darius conducted a channel from the Nile. Along the line stretching from the land of the Persians to Phoenicia, the country is broad and the space abundant; but after Phoenicia this peninsula runs along the shore of our Sea, past Palestine, Syria, and Egypt, where it ends; and in it there are only three nations.
